caveats: One laptop that was noisy all day (host round trips 8 to 34 ms p50, p99 over 400 ms; the caller p95 of the three baseline runs was 0.8 s, 1.2 s and 6.1 s). The numbers say nothing about CI runners or production.

Only two clean runs were checked against the baseline that did not help record them (the second through ci-regression.sh: p99 30 ms, worst delay 51 ms, no window over 250 ms, exit 0), so the false-alarm rate is NOT measured. The three recorded runs passing their own baseline is not evidence.
The detection proof is one injected shape (300 ms every 5 s, nearly every window). A rarer or shorter block is not shown to be caught; apiLoopP99Ms does not move for a single block per window.
The caller p95 was not judged in any run: the recorded runs disagree by more than their median, so the gate declines to use it.
Two earlier attempts at this series ran while 46 test containers used the CPU; one run aborted because the API took over 10 minutes to become ready. Those are not in the baseline.
